comments.text: Installs the road table pointers $3327 and $3467, patches the colour source $3557 and sets the script and scenery table pointers to $1677 and $1742.
Fourteen glyphs copied by the stage prologue into $79CE–$79DB. The dashboard uses the installed short message.

Round 10 stores 67 traffic type values followed by $FF. The $A748 cursor advances when an object wraps forward and moves back when the opposite depth boundary is crossed. The prologue can use the first five entries to seed visible traffic.
Round 10 stores one swap selector per traffic spawn position. Zero leaves the sprite bank in place. The respawn loop passes a nonzero selector to $9B76.
20 little-endian behavior routine addresses. The stage doubles the object type, copies the selected word to $02/$03, and calls the engine dispatcher at $89FE.
The stage uses an even offset for the low byte of each traffic handler. The adjacent high-byte load uses this base plus the same even offset.

20 little-endian addresses of sprite composition tables. The projection code at $1367 indexes by twice the traffic object type. Shared traffic and stage-specific vehicles can point to different tables.
The upper bytes of the projection-table pointers are read using this base and twice the type number. The paired low bytes are one address earlier.
The stage copies these 20 values into $A755 for the corresponding traffic objects. The projection assigns that value to each emitted sprite component at $A818.
Per-type flag loaded into $A767 before projection. When set, the projector may select an alternate shape list using the frame flash state.
Initial values copied into both $A76D and $A773 for the traffic type. The shot response decrements $A76D and uses the retained value when scoring.

Four final shape slots in the stage’s low-bank sprite block, from $30 at $CC00 to $33 at $CCC0.
Sprite area for VIC indices $88–$97, sixteen 64-byte slots. The raster multiplexer writes the shape indices of scheduled objects to both pointer tables.
Shape slots $98–$A7 continue the second stage sprite block. Slots $A0–$A7 also occupy the first half of the character memory selected by the dashboard split.
Eight sprite slots $A8–$AF in the last two pages of the replacement upper sprite block.
Stage 10 replaces the road character set starting at glyph $39. This segment reaches the penultimate complete glyph slot and the opening byte of slot $FF.
Upper half of the road character set. Groups of eight bytes give the timed road display its cell rows. The load’s final byte is at $FFF8 and the CPU uses the final hardware vector bytes separately.
